message: Could you apply the raw child’s approach, as reported by Rohin—carry unfinished work forward and check what happened—to Whisker’s next moment? What deserves closer attention in her response, guided by your intention rather than mine? Would more thinking clarify what you want readers to notice, or would trying one new sentence give better evidence? What thinking or writing step do you choose next, and could you do it rather than request permission again? What observation in the passage would make you change that choice? What finding from your draft, uncertainty, and unfinished next step will you carry into the following turn?
